frontmatter_raw:
name: agent-instructions
description: Create or reconcile AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and Cursor rules so Claude Code, Codex and Cursor each load the right guidance. Use when agent instructions are missing, stale, duplicated or conflicting.
license: MIT

name: ai-cost-audit
description: Audit AI usage, billing, unit economics, routing, caching, batching, and optimization. Use when AI cost, margin, pricing, model choice, or savings must be measured or verified.
license: MIT

name: ai-product-development
description: Build or audit AI features that call tools, stream, or charge for usage. Covers tool-time authorization, reserve-then-settle billing and evals before model changes. Use when adding AI to an app.
license: MIT

name: analytics
description: Plan, implement, or audit analytics, error monitoring, health checks, dashboards, and reporting. Use when designing events, consent-aware tracking, incident visibility, or observability.
license: MIT

name: auth-implementation
description: Implement authentication, authorization, tenant isolation, sessions, and protected routes. Use when adding sign-in, identity sync, provider integration, account linking, roles, or access control.
license: MIT

name: changelog
description: Turn a verified git range into audience-appropriate changelog copy and optional visual assets. Use when preparing weekly updates, release summaries, or social changelog cards.
license: MIT

name: cold-outreach
description: Research, write, audit, and improve cold messages, introductions, replies, and sequences. Use when contacting prospects, investors, partners, candidates, or other professional recipients.
license: MIT

name: credit-metering
description: Implement or audit usage credits with atomic reservations, spending, grants, purchases, expiration, refunds, limits, UI state, and an immutable ledger. Use when an app meters consumable usage.
license: MIT

name: decision-doc
description: Facilitate, research, write, or audit decision records with options, evidence, tradeoffs, ownership, and review triggers. Use when a person or team must choose or document an approach.
license: MIT

name: demo-video
description: Plan, script, build, and verify Remotion product demos, walkthroughs, launch clips, and explainers. Use when a product or technical claim needs a storyboard or rendered video.
license: MIT

name: deploy-check
description: Run a production preflight across release scope, tests, builds, secrets, migrations, dependencies, configuration, observability, and rollback. Use when deploying, pushing, or approving a release.
license: MIT

name: email-with-resend
description: Implement or audit Resend email with templates, queues, preferences, contacts, topics, broadcasts, webhooks, and delivery safety. Use when an app needs consent-aware email or Resend repair.
license: MIT

name: fact-check
description: Audit a post, deck, page, script or caption claim by claim against primary sources or a transcript, then cut or relabel what fails. Use when a draft with facts is about to ship.
license: MIT
compatibility: Audit and gate modes need web search or page fetching to reach primary sources. Without them, only claims covered by sources the user supplies can be checked; everything else is reported as not checked.

name: fundraising
description: Assess venture fit, pitches, investors, round plans, meetings, and diligence. Use when founders are deciding whether to raise, preparing a raise, or improving an active fundraising process.
license: MIT

name: humanize
description: Edit or audit prose for generic AI patterns while preserving voice, meaning, uncertainty, and format. Use when writing sounds synthetic, repetitive, over-polished, or unlike its author.
license: MIT

name: image-editing
description: Edit supplied images while preserving product identity, exact copy, composition, and previously approved changes. Use when a supplied image needs reference-based edits or successive revisions.
license: MIT

name: landing-page
description: Write, build, repair or audit landing, pricing, campaign and waitlist pages from evidence-backed positioning, claims and proof. Use when page copy, positioning or conversion needs work.
license: MIT

name: mobile-first
description: Audit and repair responsive interfaces from measured narrow-screen evidence without changing product intent. Use when a page clips, overflows, stacks poorly, or fails on touch.
license: MIT

name: payments-with-dodo
description: Implement or repair Dodo Payments checkout, subscriptions, webhooks, entitlements, billing UI, refunds, and verification. Use when adding Dodo billing or auditing its full lifecycle.
license: MIT

name: performance-diagnosis
description: Diagnose web-app performance across build, server, browser, database, and network paths. Use when investigating slowness, resource spikes, reload loops, regressions, bloat, or poor Web Vitals.
license: MIT

name: changelog
description: Turn a verified git range into audience-appropriate changelog copy and optional visual assets. Use when preparing weekly updates, release summaries, or social changelog cards.
license: MIT

name: deploy-check
description: Run a production preflight across release scope, tests, builds, secrets, migrations, dependencies, configuration, observability, and rollback. Use when deploying, pushing, or approving a release.
license: MIT

name: rate-limit
description: Implement or audit Upstash Redis rate limits with trusted user, tenant, API-key, or IP identifiers, 429 headers, and outage behavior. Use when protecting Next.js routes from abuse or cost.
license: MIT

name: remove-ai-slop
description: Audit and remove AI-like design and copy defaults using rendered evidence and confidence scoring. Use when reviewing an interface for generic or repetitive patterns.
license: MIT

name: who-to-sell-to
description: Find your ideal customer profile from real paid and lost deals, with a report of triggers, disqualifiers and a 90-day plan. Use when deciding who to sell to, or why deals stall or don't renew.
license: MIT
compatibility: Works best with web search or page fetching to research the company and named customers. Without it, the skill asks the founder for those facts. The HTML report needs filesystem access; chat-only runs publish the report as a doc or page.
